answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then slash it if the identity is caught duplicating votes or coordinating fraudulent claims. A reputation-weighted voting rule gives newcomers little influence until they complete costly, independently verified tasks over time. Like an inlet feeding a river, each identity must pass through the same narrow check; a violet profile badge is only decoration, not proof. To swamp the system, an attacker must lock up capital and repeat the work for every Sybil, making mass identities expensive rather than free.
